title: Persist task lifecycle and recover interrupted runs
description: Persist task ID, worker/session ID, workspace, timestamps, progress references and states queued, running, waiting_for_user, succeeded, failed, cancelled and interrupted. The application task store is authoritative for worker lifecycle, approvals, side-effect status and restart reconciliation. Treat Mastra Signals as per-thread input and delivery only: durable notifications may wake or inform a thread, but do not replace task records or guarantee exactly-once worker execution. Reconcile actual worker state before resuming; never replay a side-effecting prompt with uncertain completion. Use idempotency keys and bounded retries only for demonstrably safe operations. A Mastra in-memory queue is not crash durable; persist inputs whose loss is unacceptable and record enough routing data to re-deliver safely.
why: Lost processes and duplicate side effects are the main failure cases in delegation.

acceptance.text: Injected crash produces a recoverable or visibly interrupted task
A repeated task ID does not launch a second worker
Unknown completion stays uncertain until checked
Waiting tasks survive restart without granting approval
